drop: R is split at the reboot — the exporter's epoch boundary (FSW time falls back by > 1 s), not at any UUT event
the checker records the elapsed value in its notes

purpose.L0-1: Confirms the driver identified the device at startup and left the status register in the expected idle state.
purpose.L0-2: Proves the marker command round-trips through the command path so every later window can be bracketed.
purpose.L2-1: Writes a 64-byte pattern at offset 0 and reads it back to prove the basic write/read path and the completion counters.
purpose.L2-2: Writes and verifies the last 64 bytes of the array and shows that a request one byte past the end is rejected OUT_OF_RANGE.
purpose.L2-3: Shows that completions are returned on the port index that made the request.
purpose.L2-5: Writes and verifies every chunk of the device in one chained sweep.
purpose.L3-1: Shows that data written before an MCU reset is still intact after it, and that the reboot is visible in the record.
purpose.L5-1: Shows that a second request issued while a transfer is in progress is rejected BUSY without a completion.
purpose.L5-2: Shows that zero-length and over-size requests are rejected OUT_OF_RANGE without a completion.
purpose.L5-3: Shows that a request issued from inside a completion callback is accepted.
purpose.L6-1: Negative control: the verifier reports 64 mismatches when the read-back seed is wrong.
purpose.L7-1: Leaves a known image in the last 256 bytes and dumps it so the auditor can regenerate and compare it independently.

REQ-FramDriver-023.verification: L3-1, L3-2 (non-volatility — one-off, verification method Inspection; datasheet 002-26764 Rev.*D §Features)
